subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw expose cross-gateway session routing as a core model-visible session-tool surface now, and if so must it be named-peer-only rather than raw `gatewayUrl`?
rationale: This crosses gateway trust boundaries and changes session/message routing semantics; automation can fix individual bugs but cannot choose the permanent federation/security model.

options.title: Require named-peer design first
options.body: Pause merge until maintainers approve a named peer contract that preserves URL allowlisting, explicit credentials, idempotency, and live proof.

options.title: Narrow this PR to configured peers
options.body: Allow this branch to continue only if raw `gatewayUrl` is removed and `gateway.peers` is validated through the existing gateway tool policy.

options.title: Sponsor arbitrary URL routing
options.body: Accept a larger new security boundary by documenting and testing raw URL/token routing as an intentional operator-controlled capability.

recommendation.title: Require named-peer design first
recommendation.body: Pause merge until maintainers approve a named peer contract that preserves URL allowlisting, explicit credentials, idempotency, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history points to this person on the gateway/session/protocol files that define the affected boundary.
